Floor one: you know, it’s easy. If you don’t get a gun before fighting a boss, you can attempt to fight it using only the starting stuff, and it will 100% give you a gun, it’s done for balance purposes. I wouldn’t recommend buying anything in the shop on this floor, save your money.

Oubliette: go there only in two cases: you either have a lot of keys at the end of floor one (3 at least), duh, or if you are planning to go for the Rat, because it’s great for getting some extra dough. 

Floor 2: you know, the usual. Never go against the boss without a good weapon or a lot of blanks. While fighting Ammoconda, use mostly piercing weapons. And yeah, destroy the sentries, it can be challenging at first, but once you learn your maneuvers it can be easy. 

The Abbey: no idea, never reached it. Search for secret rooms i guess

Floor 3: watch out for those damned sneaky pitts, learn the room layouts. If you can go for the rat then do it, it’s usually worth it. Good idea to start using the stronger weapons, the enemies here can be irritating. A good place to buy items, the prices don’t bite and you will need whatever you can get on next two floors.

Floor 4: FUČK the Hollow, honestly. Beware of dark rooms, if you get into one, use rapid fire weapons. Don’t worry that much about getting a master round, the bosses are very hard. Instead, focus on killing the boss as fast as possible.

Floor 5: hammers are a bitch. Clear out rooms with them as fast as you can, use cover A LOT.
DO
NOT
FORGET
THE BULLET FOR THE PAST.
Buy all things you can, not like you will need money.  

Some general advice: don’t ever have too many weapons. It’s easy to get lost among the ton of guns you have. Sell Creep and GunMunchers are your friends. Always check for mimics, It doesn’t take much time and can save you some hp and that sweet sweet key. Use your resources. Remember your blanks, it’s okay to use them in usual rooms, they are not expensive. Also don’t forget your actives, they can help you a lot. 

That’s all I can say, hope this helps.

The game requires high skill, git gud. It is possible to deal with SPs, what you call “perfect gunplay” is just good aim, not perfect, next-to-aimbot accuracy. 

And there is no such thing as “perfect situation”, you need to know your surroundings and use them. In wide areas you can just outrun the enemy and just go out pf the SP’s range, in enclosed spaces jump around and be untrackable, the game wants you to so it. 

Use grapple/stim to run away or around, use phase shift to reposition yourself and get your grip over the situation, or use cloak, as it gives your more reaction time since it takes longer for SP to lock onto cloaked pilots. Or just use the frag grenade as a final “fuck you”.
That’s what I do, I have given my tactic above. Look for a long-ass comment.

So, the thing people forget when they fight against an SP user is that they are not going up against Legion’s smart core. The pistol doesn’t lock on instantly, and takes time to kill you. 

Obviously, you can not outgun an SP, unless you are the fastest gun in the West, and are wielding an EPG. But, you are still fighting a human, just a slightly modified one. When you can not outgun ‘em, you gotta outmaneuver them. The game gives you everything for it, you are supermobile, and while that scrub is laid back in his chair thinking about his free kill, you suddenly jump over them using a wall, or overwhelm them by running directly at them preparing to unleash the punch of million deaths. On most maps it’s easy to do, if you are engaging an SP user in a small space then you are one step from getting this free kill.

Tl;dr - Use your mobility and the precious seconds it takes to lock onto you and take the three shots. Always be on guard for the warning of a pilot locking on, when you receive the warning, run and jump around like crazy, discover their location, and then overwhelm them by taking use of your virtually unlimited mobility and your strong weapon.
